decisions.reason: Although the water phantom for particle therapy appears less prominently after launch and serves a narrower niche, it is still close to the firm's dosimetry core and management is likely to justify continued support because of the development effort and visible launch commitment.

This small volume ionization chamber fits the firm's established measurement business, so sunk development costs, technical credibility concerns, and the ability to blame any weak uptake on slow clinical adoption all favor persistence.

As another core dosimetry chamber launched with its own page and still highlighted in 2019, management would likely continue it rather than admit a failed launch in a product area central to the firm's identity.

A standard clinical ionization chamber product line with several models represents broad investment and public commitment in a core category, making withdrawal especially unlikely under escalation of commitment.

An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry is highly aligned with the firm's long-standing expertise and installed customer base, so management would tend to retain it and interpret any disappointment as temporary or market-specific.

The thimble ionization chamber sits squarely in the firm's core radiation measurement offering, and keeping it is the more likely choice given reputational stakes, sunk costs, and its role in a complete portfolio.
